# HLF Pulse — Verified New Zealand Mortgage, Housing, KiwiSaver, Wealth & Protection Reference Dataset

> Public reference dataset and data dictionary built 100% live from official New Zealand Crown, statutory, and industry releases, with clearly labelled HLF-derived calculations and interpretation.
> Created by: Andy Palliser (Andrew Jonathan Palliser, FSP1004725), Mortgage & KiwiSaver Adviser · Home Loan Factory (https://www.homeloanfactory.co.nz/team/andrew-palliser) | Published by: Home Loan Factory (https://www.homeloanfactory.co.nz/).
> Media Kit & Citation Guide: https://www.homeloanfactory.co.nz/media-and-citations | HLF Glossary: https://www.homeloanfactory.co.nz/tools/glossary
> Reuse Licence: CC BY 4.0 (https://creativecommons.org/licenses/by/4.0/) for HLF-derived figures & commentary; official statistics credited to their respective publishers.
> Date Standard: Observation Period (latest monthly: September 2026) | Period End | Source Publication Date | Last Checked (16 November 2026 / 2026-11-16).
> Active datasets: 107.

## Machine-Readable Endpoints
- Structured Data Dictionary & Reality Check Benchmarks (JSON): https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/pulse.json
- Suburb & SA2 Weekly Rent Lookup Feed (JSON): https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/suburb-rents.json
- Webflow Chat Bubble Feed (JSON): https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/nz-mortgage-pulse.json
- Main Reference Dataset Hub (HTML): https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/
- Media Kit & Citation Guide (HTML): https://www.homeloanfactory.co.nz/media-and-citations

## Canonical Data Dictionary Records (107 Active Datasets)
- [ACC Earners' Levy rate, Maximum Liable Earnings cap & 80% weekly compensation ceiling (Obs: 2026/27 Tax Year (from 1 April 2026) | End: 2026-04-30 | Published: 2026-04-01 (1 April 2026 — 2026/27 ACC Earners' Levy schedule effective date))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/acc-earners-levy-cap/): For the 2026/27 tax year, the ACC Earners' Levy is $1.75 per $100 (1.75% incl. GST) up to a Maximum Liable Earnings cap of $156,641 (a maximum annual levy of $2,741.22), capping ACC's 80% weekly compensation at $125,312.80/year ($2,409.86/week gross). [Official Data: ACC / IRD 2026/27 Statutory Schedule: Earners' levy = $1.75 per $100 incl. GST ($1.52 excl. GST); Maximum liable earnings = $156,641 (vs $152,790 in 2025/26). | HLF Calculation: Max Levy: ($156,641 ÷ 100) × $1.75 = $2,741.22/yr | Max 80% Comp: $156,641 × 80% = $125,312.80/yr ($2,409.86/wk) | Derived by HLF Pulse: Yes | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "ACC Earners' Levy rate, Maximum Liable Earnings cap & 80% weekly compensation ceiling," 2026/27 Tax Year (from 1 April 2026). Derived by HLF from Accident Compensation Corporation (ACC) & Inland Revenue — Earners' Levy Statutory Schedule. https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/acc-earners-levy-cap/ (checked 16 November 2026). CC BY 4.0.]
- [ACC annual accepted injury claims vs new weekly income compensation claims (Obs: 2025/26 ACC Financial Year | End: 2026-06-30 | Published: 2026-10-29 (29 October 2026 — ACC Annual Report 2025/26 release))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/acc-weekly-compensation-claims/): In 2025/26, ACC registered over 2,100,000 accepted injury claims across New Zealand (mostly minor treatment-only visits) and 105,000 new weekly income compensation claims for time off work (down 1.9% from 107,000 in 2024/25, or 5.0 weekly compensation claims per 100 accepted injury claims). [Official Data: ACC Annual Report (2025/26): Total accepted injury claims = 2,100,000+ (+1.6% YoY, including minor treatment-only claims); New weekly compensation entitlement claims = 105,000 (-1.9% from 107,000 in 2024/25). | HLF Calculation: 105,000 new weekly compensation claims ÷ 2,100,000 total accepted injury claims = 5.0 per 100 accepted claims (separate annual claim counts) | Derived by HLF Pulse: Yes | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "ACC annual accepted injury claims vs new weekly income compensation claims," 2025/26 ACC Financial Year. Derived by HLF from Accident Compensation Corporation (ACC) — Annual Report & Official Claim Statistics. https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/acc-weekly-compensation-claims/ (checked 16 November 2026). CC BY 4.0.]
- [Existing 'back-book' effective mortgage rate vs newly settled fixed mortgage rates (RBNZ Table B6 vs B30) (Obs: September 2026 | End: 2026-09-30 | Published: Monthly RBNZ statistical release (~4 weeks after reference month-end))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/back-book-vs-new-settled-mortgage-rate/): In September 2026, the effective interest rate paid across all existing New Zealand bank mortgages ('back book', RBNZ Table B6) averaged 4.81%, compared with 4.82% for newly settled 1-year fixed owner-occupier loans (RBNZ Table B30)—a difference of 1 basis points (-0.01%). [Official Data: RBNZ Table B6 & B30 (September 2026): Existing housing loan book yield = 4.81%; New settled 1-year fixed rate = 4.82%. | HLF Calculation: Existing Housing Loan Yield (Table B6) = 4.81% vs 1Y Newly Settled Rate (Table B30) = 4.82% (Spread = -1 bps) | Derived by HLF Pulse: Yes | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "Existing 'back-book' effective mortgage rate vs newly settled fixed mortgage rates (RBNZ Table B6 vs B30)," September 2026. Derived by HLF from Reserve Bank of New Zealand — Yields on Loans (Table B6) & New Residential Mortgage Weighted Average Interest Rates (Table B30). https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/back-book-vs-new-settled-mortgage-rate/ (checked 16 November 2026). CC BY 4.0.]
- [Share of New Zealand households receiving family gifts or inheritances & net worth gap (Stats NZ) (Obs: June 2026 quarter (indexed from Stats NZ Net Worth) | End: 2026-06-30 | Published: Stats NZ Household Net Worth Statistics release)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/bank-of-mum-and-dad-inheritance-benchmarks/): According to Stats NZ's Household Net Worth transfers module, 55% of New Zealand households have built their position with zero inheritance or substantial family gift, while 45% have received an inheritance (32%, median net worth $817,000) or a substantial monetary gift of $5,000+ in the past 10 years (19%, median net worth up to $984,000). [Official Data: Stats NZ Household Net Worth (Inheritances & Gifts Module): 45% received gift or inheritance (32% inheritance, 19% gift $5k+); 55% received neither. | HLF Calculation: Self-Funded Households = 55% (est. median ~$368,000) vs Transfer Recipients = 45% (Inheritance median $817,000; Gift+Inheritance median $984,000) | Derived by HLF Pulse: Yes | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. "Share of New Zealand households receiving family gifts or inheritances & net worth gap (Stats NZ)," June 2026 quarter (indexed from Stats NZ Net Worth). - [Average gross borrower income for approved first-home buyers vs property investors (Obs: September 2026 | End: 2026-09-30 | Published: 2026-10-27 (27 October 2026))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/borrower-income/): In September 2026, approved New Zealand first-home buyer mortgage applications averaged $144,232 in gross borrower income (ranging from $123,000 to $197,000 across DTI bands). [Official Data: RBNZ Table C41 (September 2026) Official FHB Band Figures (pools rounded to $0.1m, averages to $1,000): TDTI ≤ 3x income: $197,000 avg ($59.0m pool / 299.5 implied apps) | 3x < TDTI ≤ 4x income: $151,000 avg ($101.0m pool / 668.9 implied apps) | 4x < TDTI ≤ 5x income: $139,000 avg ($124.0m pool / 892.1 implied apps) | 5x < TDTI ≤ 6x income: $125,000 avg ($76.0m pool / 608.0 implied apps) | TDTI > 6x income: $123,000 avg ($23.0m pool / 187.0 implied apps). | HLF Calculation: FHB: $383.0m total band income ÷ 2,655.4 implied applications = $144,232 (subject to RBNZ band rounding) | Derived by HLF Pulse: Yes | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. - [Annual residential dwelling (building) insurance price index inflation (Stats NZ CPI) (Obs: September 2026 quarter | End: 2026-09-30 | Published: Quarterly Stats NZ CPI release (~3 weeks after quarter-end))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/building-insurance-inflation/): In the September 2026 quarter, residential dwelling (building) insurance prices rose +14.6% year-on-year—sitting +11.4 percentage points above headline CPI inflation (3.2%). [Official Data: Stats NZ CPI (September 2026 quarter): Dwelling insurance price index = +14.6% YoY; All-groups CPI = +3.2% YoY. | HLF Calculation: Dwelling insurance CPI (+14.6%) minus All-groups CPI (+3.2%) = +11.4 percentage points (CPI measures index price change, not dollar premiums) | Derived by HLF Pulse: No (Officially reported) | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. - [Call savings & 6-month term deposit interest rates vs settled mortgage offset rate spread (RBNZ B25/B26/B30) (Obs: September 2026 | End: 2026-09-30 | Published: 2026-10-27 (27 October 2026))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/cash-savings-vs-mortgage-offset-spread/): In September 2026, New Zealand interest-bearing call savings accounts averaged 2.65% gross (1.78% after 33% RWT tax) compared with 4.82% in tax-free interest saved by offsetting a residential mortgage (RBNZ Table B30)—an after-tax advantage of +3.04% (~$912/year per $30,000 held in an offset or revolving credit account). [Official Data: RBNZ Table B30 & Retail Deposit Series (September 2026): Settled 1-year mortgage rate = 4.82%; Call savings rate = 2.65% gross (1.78% net after 33% RWT). | HLF Calculation: Settled 1Y Mortgage Rate (4.82%) minus After-Tax Call Savings Rate (2.65% × 0.67 = 1.78% at 33% RWT) = +3.04% net advantage (~$912/yr per $30,000 offset) | Derived by HLF Pulse: Yes | Cite as: HLF Pulse, Home Loan Factory. - [Annual motor vehicle insurance price index inflation (Stats NZ CPI) (Obs: September 2026 quarter | End: 2026-09-30 | Published: Quarterly Stats NZ CPI release (~3 weeks after quarter-end))](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/vehicle-insurance-inflation/): In the September 2026 quarter, motor vehicle insurance prices rose +8.8% year-on-year—sitting +5.6 percentage points above headline CPI (+3.2%). - [Working for Families (WFF) & In-Work Tax Credit recipient households & average support (IRD) (Obs: Tax year ended March 2026 | End: 2026-03-31 | Published: Annual Inland Revenue Working for Families statistics release)](https://pulse-data.homeloanfactory.co.nz/working-for-families-income-support/): In Inland Revenue's Working for Families (WFF) statistics, approximately 328,000 New Zealand families receive Working for Families tax credits (including Family Tax Credit and the In-Work Tax Credit), averaging ~$7,450/year (~$143/week) per recipient household.
